r1159104365: Straddles the equator and the prime meridian, bordered by the Mediterranean Sea, the Atlantic and Indian Oceans.
Has the youngest population of any continent and is home to the greatest diversity of megafauna species.
Contains 54 sovereign states; Algeria is the largest by area and Nigeria the largest by population.
Highly vulnerable to climate change, facing desertification, deforestation and water scarcity.
r1159104289: An archipelago of about 7,641 islands in the western Pacific, divided into Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao.
Named after King Philip II of Spain after Ferdinand Magellan's arrival began Spanish colonization.
Passed from Spanish to American control after 1898, was occupied by Japan in WWII, and gained independence in 1946.
r1730072397: A Melanesian archipelago of more than 330 islands, formed mostly by volcanic activity starting around 150 million years ago.
Most people live on the two largest islands, Viti Levu and Vanua Levu, with the capital Suva on Viti Levu.
Became a British colony in 1874 and gained independence in 1970, later experiencing several coups.
m1159115079: The largest and deepest of Earth's oceans, stretching between Asia/Australia and the Americas.
Contains the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point on Earth at 10,928 m.
Includes major marginal seas such as the South China Sea, Sea of Japan and Coral Sea.
r1159104263: The world's largest island, lying between the Arctic and Atlantic Oceans east of Canada's Arctic Archipelago.
An autonomous territory of Denmark whose capital is Nuuk; was settled by Norse colonists from the 10th century.
Politically tied to Norway for centuries before coming under Danish rule in 1814.
vQ3392: Flows north through northeast Africa into the Mediterranean Sea, formed by the White Nile and Blue Nile meeting at Khartoum.
Was the foundation of Ancient Egyptian civilization, whose annual floods deposited fertile silt along its banks.
Its source near Lake Victoria was a major goal of 19th-century European exploration.
Geologically young, having followed its present course for only about 15,000 years.
m1159115017: The smallest, shallowest and coldest of the world's oceans, centered on the North Pole.
Surrounded by Eurasia and North America, bordered by the Bering Strait and the Greenland-Scotland Ridge.
Covered by sea ice most of the year, with satellite records showing a continuous decline in ice extent.
r1159102961: A North Atlantic archipelago between Iceland, Norway and Scotland, and an autonomous territory of Denmark.
Rugged terrain of fjords and cliffs, first settled by Norse people in the early 9th century.
Capital Tórshavn receives fewer recorded hours of sunshine than any other city in the world.
p1159104871: A small island in the southern Caribbean, lying on the South American continental shelf north of Venezuela.
Became a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands in 1986, with Oranjestad as its capital.
Has an arid, sunny climate unlike the humid tropics typical of much of the Caribbean.
r1159103491: A Spanish archipelago off northwest Africa, an autonomous community with capitals in Santa Cruz de Tenerife and Las Palmas.
Popular year-round destination thanks to a mild, sunny climate despite its Atlantic location.
m1159115521: An inlet of the Indian Ocean between the Arabian Peninsula and Africa, connected via the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait.
Lies above the Red Sea Rift, part of the Great Rift Valley, and leads north to the Suez Canal.
Mostly shallow, with extensive shelves supporting over 1,000 invertebrate species and 200 types of coral.
vQ626: The longest river in Europe, flowing through Central and Southern Russia into the landlocked Caspian Sea.
Widely regarded as Russia's national river and celebrated in literature and folklore as "Mother Volga".
Five of Russia's ten largest cities, including Moscow, lie within its drainage basin.
p1159104855: An island in the Lesser Antilles of the eastern Caribbean, an overseas department and region of France.
Mount Pelée and the Pitons du Carbet were listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023.
Part of the European Union as an outermost region, though outside the Schengen Area.
l1159113127: A rift lake in southern Siberia, Russia, and the deepest lake in the world at 1,642 m.
Holds about 22-23% of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water, more than all the Great Lakes combined.
The world's oldest lake at 25-30 million years, home to many species found nowhere else.
Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996.
r1730070893: A self-governing coral island in Polynesia, in free association with New Zealand and nicknamed "The Rock".
Terrain rises from a coastal terrace to a limestone plateau about 60 m above sea level.
Most Niueans live in New Zealand, far outnumbering those on the island itself.
r1159103787: One of the Greater Sunda Islands in Indonesia, bordered by the Indian Ocean and the Java Sea.
The world's most populous island, home to over half of Indonesia's population on just 7% of its land.
Formed by volcanic eruptions from subduction of the Australian Plate, giving it a spine of volcanic mountains.
Was the center of Hindu-Buddhist empires, Islamic sultanates and Dutch colonial rule.
vQ5413: The longest river in China, rising in the Tibetan Plateau and flowing east to the East China Sea.
Its drainage basin covers a fifth of China's land and houses nearly a third of its population.
The Three Gorges Dam on the river is the largest hydroelectric power station in the world.
Home to the now-extinct Yangtze river dolphin and the critically endangered Yangtze sturgeon.
r1730073279: A Mediterranean archipelago off Spain's eastern coast, an autonomous community with Palma as its capital.
Divided into the western Pityusic Islands (Ibiza, Formentera) and eastern Gymnesian Islands (Mallorca, Menorca).
Ibiza is known worldwide for its electronic music and nightclub scene.
l1159113191: Africa's largest lake by area and the world's largest tropical lake, shared by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.
Home to many fish species found nowhere else, especially cichlids, though invasive Nile perch have driven some to extinction.
m1159117285: The world's largest coral reef system, made up of over 2,900 reefs and 900 islands off Queensland, Australia.
Built by billions of tiny coral polyps, it is the largest structure on Earth made by living organisms and visible from space.
Has lost more than half its coral cover since 1985 due to bleaching, pollution and cyclone damage.
Long used by Aboriginal Australian and Torres Strait Islander peoples and now a major tourism draw.
r1159102581: A dependent territory of New Zealand made up of three coral atolls in the southern Pacific.
The first nation in the world to be powered entirely by solar energy.
Has one of the smallest populations and economies of any country or territory.
r1159103851: A Norwegian archipelago in the Arctic Ocean, about midway between mainland Norway and the North Pole.
The Svalbard Treaty of 1920 gave Norway sovereignty while keeping it a demilitarized free economic zone.
Home to the Svalbard Global Seed Vault and about 60% covered by glaciers.
l1159113185: The world's longest freshwater lake and second-deepest after Lake Baikal, shared by Tanzania, the DRC, Burundi and Zambia.
Drains via the Lukuga and Congo rivers into the Atlantic Ocean.
r1159104333: The world's largest peninsula, occupying most of the Arabian plate between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.
Mostly covered by the Arabian Desert, an extension of the Sahara.
United politically and religiously under Prophet Muhammad in the 7th century AD.
Formed between 56 and 23 million years ago by the Red Sea Rift splitting the African and Arabian plates.
m1159115273: A marginal sea of the western Pacific bounded by China, the Indochinese Peninsula and the Philippines.
One of the world's busiest shipping routes, carrying over $3 trillion in trade in 2016.
Its scattered islands and reefs are subject to competing sovereignty claims by several countries.
vQ34589: The longest river in West Asia, rising in Turkey and flowing through Syria and Iraq to join the Tigris.
Together with the Tigris, it defines Mesopotamia, the historic "land between the rivers".
m1159115343: A region of the northern Indian Ocean bounded by the Arabian Peninsula, Pakistan, India and Somalia.
The Straits of Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb at its ends have linked Old World trade networks since the 3rd millennium BC.
Trade here was historically governed by seasonal monsoon winds.
p1159105019: A group of three waterfalls on the Niagara River between Ontario, Canada and New York, USA.
Horseshoe Falls, the largest and most powerful by flow rate in North America, straddles the border.
Formed when glaciers receded at the end of the last ice age, carving through the Niagara Escarpment.
A major source of hydroelectric power and a popular honeymoon destination.
l1159113279: A high-altitude lake in the Andes on the border of Peru and Bolivia, often called the world's highest navigable lake.
South America's largest lake by both volume and surface area, with slightly brackish water.
vQ1471: Rises near Dijon in northeastern France and flows through Paris to the English Channel at Le Havre.
Navigable by ocean-going vessels as far as Rouen, and crossed in Paris by 37 bridges including the Pont Neuf.
m1159116535: An arm of the Atlantic Ocean separating southern England from northern France, the world's busiest shipping area.
Narrows to just 34 km wide at the Strait of Dover, its northeastern end linking to the North Sea.
Helped the United Kingdom resist invasion, including during the Napoleonic Wars and World War II.
m1159117067: A narrow strait connecting the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea, separating Europe from Africa.
Narrows to just 14 km between Spain and Morocco, crossed by ferry in as little as 35 minutes.
Lies in the territorial waters of Morocco, Spain and the British territory of Gibraltar.
xQ16990: An active stratovolcano on Sicily's east coast, the tallest peak in Italy south of the Alps.
One of the world's most active volcanoes, in an almost constant state of activity, designated a Decade Volcano.
Its fertile volcanic soils support vineyards and orchards on its lower slopes.
Became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013.
m1159116697: An elongated bay of the Mediterranean Sea between southern Italy, Albania and western Greece.
Home to Calypso Deep, the deepest point in the Mediterranean at 5,109 m.
One of the most seismically active maritime areas in the world.
r1159103791: The largest and most populous island in the Philippines, home to the capital Manila.
Economic and political center of the country, with over half of the Philippines' population.
r1159103803: Russia's largest island, lying in the Sea of Okhotsk off the coast of Khabarovsk Krai near Hokkaido, Japan.
Contested for centuries between China, Russia and Japan; split between Russia and Japan after the 1905 Russo-Japanese War.
Has been entirely under Russian control since the final days of World War II in 1945.
r1159103741: A steep canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, over a mile deep and up to 18 miles wide.
Exposes nearly two billion years of geological history as the river cut through the uplifting Colorado Plateau.
Has been inhabited by Native Americans for thousands of years, who considered it a holy site.
vQ6862: Forms the natural border between the Russian Far East and Northeast China, also known as the Heilong River.
Home to the kaluga, a sturgeon that is one of the largest freshwater fish in the world at up to 5.6 m long.
e1159108719: The highest mountain outside Asia, located in Argentina's Andes, and one of the Seven Summits.
Formed by subduction of the Nazca Plate and was once an active stratovolcano before activity stopped in the Miocene.
First climbed in 1897, it is technically straightforward but its extreme altitude earns it the nickname "Mountain of Death."
m1159116395: A southern inlet of the Barents Sea on Russia's northwest coast, entirely within Russian internal waters.
Historically Russia's main center of international maritime trade before becoming a key Soviet naval base.
One of four seas named after a common color, alongside the Black, Red and Yellow seas.
e1159105799: A dormant compound volcano in easternmost Turkey, consisting of Greater and Little Ararat.
Identified since the Middle Ages with the biblical resting place of Noah's Ark.
The principal national symbol of Armenia, depicted on its coat of arms, though located outside Armenia's borders.
vQ80240: Flows through Russia and Kazakhstan along the conventional boundary between Europe and Asia.
The third-longest river in Europe after the Volga and Danube, discharging into the Caspian Sea.
vQ43106: Africa's fourth-longest river and the largest flowing into the Indian Ocean from the continent.
Famous for Victoria Falls along its course through six southern African countries.
The Kariba and Cahora Bassa dams on it supply hydroelectric power to Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique and South Africa.
vQ5419: The longest river in the United States, rising in Montana's Rocky Mountains and joining the Mississippi near St. Louis.
Was a key route for 19th-century westward expansion, used by fur trappers and then steamboats.
Fifteen dams impound its main stem, creating some of the largest reservoirs in the US, including Lake Sakakawea.
r1159104331: The continental portion of Southeast Asia, historically known as Indochina, comprising Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia and Peninsular Malaysia.
The name Indochina reflected the historical cultural influence of India and China on the region.
m1159116027: A marginal sea of the western Pacific off eastern China, bounded by Japan's Kyushu, the Ryukyu Islands and Taiwan.
Mostly shallow, averaging 350 m deep, with the Okinawa Trough reaching 2,716 m.
Connects to the Sea of Japan, South China Sea and Philippine Sea through several straits.
l1159113163: An African Great Lake and the southernmost in the East African Rift system, shared by Malawi, Mozambique and Tanzania.
Home to more fish species than any other lake in the world, including over 700 cichlid species.
A meromictic lake, meaning its water layers remain permanently stratified rather than mixing.
m1159115959: A shallow sea on the Sunda Shelf between Borneo, Java, Sumatra and Sulawesi in Indonesia.
Linked to the South China Sea via the Karimata Strait, and sometimes classed as part of the Indian Ocean.
r1159104253: A large semiarid sandy savanna in Southern Africa, covering much of Botswana and parts of Namibia and South Africa.
e1159107857: An active stratovolcano on Tenerife in the Canary Islands and the highest point in Spain.
Measured from the ocean floor, it is the third-tallest volcanic structure on Earth.
Began forming about 170,000 years ago after a catastrophic landslide; last erupted in 1909.
Its national park is the most visited in Spain and Europe, and hosts the Teide astronomical Observatory.
m1159116359: A gulf of the Indian Ocean connecting the Arabian Sea to the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf.
Borders Iran and Pakistan to the north, Oman to the south, and the UAE to the west.
r1159104081: A desert plateau on Chile's Pacific coast, the driest non-polar desert and largest fog desert on Earth.
Shielded from rainfall by both the Andes and the Chilean Coast Range plus the cold Humboldt Current.
Its dry air and dark skies make it a premier astronomical site, hosting the ALMA and Very Large Telescope observatories.
19th-century nitrate deposits here sparked the War of the Pacific between Chile, Bolivia and Peru.
r1159103767: An archipelago at the southern tip of South America, across the Strait of Magellan, split between Chile and Argentina.
Named "Land of Fire" after fires early European explorers saw lit by its indigenous inhabitants.
Cape Horn, at its southernmost extent, lies just north of 56 degrees south latitude.
r1159103783: A large island off eastern Canada, blocking the mouth of the Saint Lawrence River to form the Gulf of Saint Lawrence.
Home to over 90% of the province of Newfoundland and Labrador's population, mostly on the Avalon Peninsula.
Cape Spear near the capital St. John's is the easternmost point in North America excluding Greenland.
e1159105823: The third-highest mountain in the world, straddling the border of Nepal and India's Sikkim state.
Was long thought to be the world's highest peak until surveys in 1849 showed Everest was taller.
First climbed in 1955 by a team that stopped short of the true summit out of respect for its sacred status.
l1159114143: A deep lake on the north side of the Alps shared between Switzerland and France, the largest on the Rhône's course.
About 60% of the lake belongs to Switzerland and 40% to France.
r1159104629: One of New Zealand's two main islands, separated from the South Island by Cook Strait.
Home to 76% of New Zealand's population and the capital Wellington, at its southwestern tip.
l1159113021: One of the five Great Lakes of North America, shared by Ontario, Canada, and Michigan, USA.
Hydrologically one body of water with Lake Michigan, together forming the largest freshwater lake by area in the world.
Water flows through it faster than any other Great Lake, with a retention time of just 22 years.
r1159104189: A mountain range in North Africa separating the Sahara from the Mediterranean and Atlantic, stretching through Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.
Its highest peak, Toubkal in Morocco, reaches 4,167 m.
Primarily inhabited by Berber populations, whose word for mountain is believed to be the origin of the name Atlas.
m1159116123: A shallow inlet of the South China Sea bounded by Mainland Southeast Asia and the Malay Peninsula.
Surrounded by Thailand, Cambodia and the Mekong Delta region of Vietnam.
l1159113095: A freshwater lake in northwestern Russia near Saint Petersburg, the largest lake located entirely in Europe.
A methane lake on Saturn's moon Titan, Ladoga Lacus, is named after it.
r1730072855: A historical region on Croatia's Adriatic coast, a narrow coastal belt backed by the rugged Dinaric Alps.
Named after the ancient Illyrian Dalmatae tribe; its largest city is Split, followed by Dubrovnik.
Was ruled in turn by Rome, Byzantium, Venice and the Habsburgs before becoming part of Croatia.
l1159114879: A freshwater lake in northeast Israel, fed mainly by the Jordan River flowing north to south through it.
The lowest freshwater lake on Earth, lying well over 200 m below sea level.
r1159104169: A mountain range in Central Asia where Russia, China, Mongolia and Kazakhstan meet, source of the Irtysh and Ob rivers.
Its highest peak, Belukha, reaches 4,506 m; the range merges southeast into the Gobi Desert plateau.
Home to a sparse, ethnically diverse population of Turkic peoples, Mongols and Volga Germans.
m1159116037: A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean between Wrangel Island, Russia and Point Barrow, Alaska.
Connected to the Pacific Ocean via the Bering Strait at its southern limit.
r1159104157: A landmass in Mainland Southeast Asia reaching the southernmost point of the Asian mainland at Tanjung Piai.
Divided by the Strait of Malacca from Sumatra, and backed by the Titiwangsa Mountains.
m1159115695: A body of water between Greenland, Svalbard and the Norwegian Sea, sometimes classed within the Arctic Ocean.
A major breeding ground for harp and hooded seals, hunted here for over 200 years.
vQ104437: A major river of northwestern North America, flowing from British Columbia through Yukon and Alaska to the Bering Sea.
The longest river in Alaska and Yukon, it was a principal transportation route during the 1896-1903 Klondike Gold Rush.
r1159104319: A broad expanse of prairie and grassland east of the Rocky Mountains, spanning the central US and western Canada.
Covers most of Kansas, Nebraska and the Dakotas along with parts of several other US states and Canadian provinces.
r1159103651: A desert in the Tarim Basin of northwestern China, ringed by the Kunlun, Pamir and Tian Shan mountains and the Gobi Desert.
m1159115197: A marginal sea of the western Pacific east of the Philippines, the largest sea in the world by surface area.
Enclosed by island arcs including the Ryukyus, Taiwan, the Philippines and the Marianas.
Home to the Philippine Trench and the Mariana Trench, containing the deepest point on Earth.
e1159105733: A mountain in Tibet near the source of four major rivers: the Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra and Ghaghara.
Considered sacred in Bon, Buddhism, Hinduism and Jainism, drawing pilgrims who circle the mountain on foot.
Has never been successfully climbed, and ascent is prohibited by China due to its religious significance.
vQ3140: Flows from the Adirondack Mountains south through eastern New York into a tidal estuary at New York Bay.
Named after Henry Hudson, who explored it in 1609 while sailing for the Dutch East India Company.
Inspired the 19th-century Hudson River School of landscape painting and early American environmentalism.
e1159105791: The ninth-highest mountain on Earth, the westernmost major peak of the Himalayas in Pakistan.
One of the 14 eight-thousanders, nicknamed "Killer Mountain" for its high number of climbing fatalities.
The fastest-growing mountain in the world, rising about 7 mm per year.
r1159104059: A coastal desert stretching along the Atlantic coasts of Angola, Namibia and South Africa.
Possibly the oldest desert in the world, having been arid for 55-80 million years.
Its dunes are the second-largest in the world, and coastal fog from the cold Benguela Current sustains desert life.
The fog has also wrecked over a thousand ships along the aptly named Skeleton Coast.
l1159113111: A lake in southeastern Kazakhstan fed mainly by the Ili River within a closed desert basin.
One of the largest lakes in Asia, but shrinking due to water diversion, much like the Aral Sea.
Split by a narrow strait into a freshwater western half and a saline eastern half.
m1159116815: An estuary formed by the Uruguay and Paraná rivers meeting between Argentina and Uruguay before reaching the Atlantic.
If classified as a river, it is the widest in the world, reaching 220 km across at its mouth.
Its shores hold the port cities of Buenos Aires and Montevideo, cradle of tango culture.
r1159104167: A mountain range spanning Iran, northern Iraq and southeastern Turkey, running to the Persian Gulf.
Its highest point, Mount Dena, reaches 4,409 m, and the range ends near the Strait of Hormuz.
l1159126655: A saline, endorheic lake in the Tian Shan mountains of eastern Kyrgyzstan.
The eighth-deepest lake in the world, which rarely freezes despite its elevation and cold winters due to its salinity.
A Ramsar wetland site of globally significant biodiversity.
m1159116589: An arm of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland, divided into the Bothnian Sea and Bothnian Bay.
The Åland Islands lie at its mouth.
vQ131574: The longest river in the Czech Republic, flowing north through Český Krumlov, České Budějovice and Prague.
A left tributary of the Elbe River, commonly called the "Czech national river".
r1159102907: A group of volcanic islands in French Polynesia in the southern Pacific, settled around the 10th century AD by West Polynesian voyagers.
Named after the 16th-century Spanish Marquis of Cañete by navigator Álvaro de Mendaña in 1595.
Known for a culture, biology and language that has stayed remarkably uniform across centuries.
m1159115771: An arm of the Indian Ocean between Madagascar and Mozambique, about 1,700 km long.
The warm Mozambique Current flows southward through it into the Agulhas Current off southern Africa.
r1159103777: Canada's northernmost and third-largest island, part of the Arctic Archipelago's Queen Elizabeth Islands.
Home to Cape Columbia, the northernmost point of land in Canada, and the Arctic Cordillera, its most mountainous range.
Had a 2021 population of just 144 people across three remote settlements.
m1159115419: An arm of the North Atlantic between the Labrador Peninsula and Greenland, connecting to Baffin Bay via the Davis Strait.
Formed as the North American and Greenland plates separated starting about 60 million years ago.
A major source of North Atlantic Deep Water, a cold water mass that circulates at great ocean depths.
r1159102955: A group of islands in the Ionian Sea west of mainland Greece, traditionally called the Heptanese, or "Seven Islands".
Kept outside Ottoman control for centuries under Venetian rule, giving them a distinct Italian-influenced culture.
Joined the modern Greek state in 1864.
m1159116947: A strait separating Taiwan from mainland China, connecting the South China Sea to the East China Sea.
Narrows to about 126 km wide at its narrowest point.
r1159103605: A mountain range in Bulgaria running from the Serbian border east to the Black Sea at Cape Emine.
Gives the Balkans their name; known in Bulgarian and Serbian as "Stara planina", or "old mountain".
Its highest peak, Botev, reaches 2,376 m, and its karst terrain holds caves with notable prehistoric cave art.
p1159104793: An uninhabited coral island near the equator in the central Pacific, part of the US Minor Outlying Islands.
Best known as the island Amelia Earhart was trying to reach when her plane disappeared in 1937.
Managed today as a strict nature reserve with no economic activity.
r1159102797: An archipelago in Norway's Nordland county known for dramatic mountains, open sea and sheltered bays.
Has unusually mild winters for its northerly latitude and attracts about a million tourists a year, many for the northern lights.
r1159104137: An archipelago of about 200 islands in the Indian Ocean southwest of Myanmar, part of India's Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
Home to the Andamanese indigenous peoples, including the Sentinelese on North Sentinel Island, whom visitors are banned from approaching.
m1159115579: A part of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica, bounded by Coats Land and the Antarctic Peninsula.
Much of its southern part is covered by the massive Filchner-Ronne Ice Shelf.
Famed for having some of the clearest water of any sea, and for trapping Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance in its ice.
r1159103737: A historical region of desert and mountains straddling Pakistan, Iran and Afghanistan, home to the ethnic Baloch people.
Significant for its mineral wealth, long Arabian Sea coastline and potential oil and gas reserves.
r1159104283: The largest of the Hawaiian Islands, nicknamed the "Big Island", in the North Pacific Ocean.
Holds 63% of the Hawaiian archipelago's land but only 13% of its population; largest city is Hilo.
m1159116269: A stretch of water between Cape Horn, Chile and Antarctica's South Shetland Islands, linking the Atlantic and Pacific.
One of the most treacherous voyages for ships, with waves regularly topping 40 feet due to the unimpeded Antarctic Circumpolar Current.
As the narrowest choke point around Antarctica, it strongly shapes global ocean circulation and climate.
m1159116907: A sea passage between the Korean Peninsula and Japan, connecting the East China Sea, Yellow Sea and Sea of Japan.
Split by Tsushima Island into western and eastern channels; a proposed undersea tunnel would link Japan and Korea.
r1159104529: A remote subantarctic archipelago in the southern Indian Ocean, part of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands.
Among the most isolated places on Earth, with no indigenous inhabitants and no airport, reachable only by ship.
l1159115833: A large freshwater loch in the Scottish Highlands, famed for claimed sightings of the "Loch Ness Monster".
Lies along the Great Glen Fault and holds more water than any other lake in Great Britain.
m1159116181: An arm of the Southern Ocean off Marie Byrd Land in western Antarctica, named after explorer Roald Amundsen.
Mostly ice-covered, fed by the Thwaites Ice Tongue draining part of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet.
r1159104233: A plateau covering much of western, central and southern India, flanked by the Eastern and Western Ghats.
Formed largely by the Deccan Traps, massive basaltic lava flows from an eruption at the end of the Cretaceous period.
Home over centuries to major Indian kingdoms including the Chalukyas, Vijayanagara Empire and the Deccan sultanates.
l1159114361: A lake in North Sumatra, Indonesia, filling the caldera of the Toba supervolcano and the largest volcanic lake in the world.
Formed by a supervolcanic eruption 69,000-77,000 years ago, among the largest explosive eruptions in the last 25 million years.
The eruption's possible global climate effects are the basis of the contested Toba catastrophe theory of human population decline.
r1730072209: The world's largest mangrove forest, spanning the Ganges Delta across Bangladesh and India's West Bengal.
Formed where the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers meet the Bay of Bengal.
Several of its protected areas are UNESCO World Heritage Sites, though it faces threats from cyclones and rising salinity.
e1159105787: An active stratovolcano on the China-North Korea border, the tallest mountain in both North Korea and Northeast China.
Its caldera holds Heaven Lake, source of the Songhua, Tumen and Yalu rivers.
Considered the mythical ancestral homeland of Korean and Manchu peoples; depicted on North Korea's national emblem.
A 946 AD eruption here was among the most powerful on Earth in the last 5,000 years.
vQ171649: The largest right-bank tributary of the Congo River, forming part of the borders of the Central African Republic, DRC and Republic of the Congo.
Flows through Bangui, the capital of the Central African Republic.
Its upper reaches once flowed into Lake Chad before being captured by the Congo system in the early Pleistocene.
r1159104293: A group of 36,563 islands north of mainland Canada, excluding Greenland and Iceland, mostly within Nunavut and the Northwest Territories.
Showing effects of climate change, with melting projected to add 3.5 cm to global sea level rise by 2100.
m1159118303: A strait between Australia's Cape York Peninsula and Papua New Guinea, also known as Zenadh Kes.
Named after Spanish navigator Luís Vaz de Torres, who sailed through it in 1606.
r1159102831: The largest and only permanently populated island of Norway's Svalbard archipelago in the Arctic Ocean.
About 58% covered in ice, with Longyearbyen as its administrative center.
First used as a 17th-18th century whaling base, later developed for coal mining under the 1920 Svalbard Treaty.
r1159104623: A mountain range running along much of New Zealand's South Island, reaching its highest points on the western side.
Its Main Divide separates the wetter west coast from the more populated eastern regions.
l1159106729: A lake in Canada's Northwest Territories, the deepest lake in North America at 614 m.
Shares its name with the Dene people, called "Slavey" by their Cree rivals.
The territorial capital Yellowknife sits on its shore.
vQ26422: A Southeast Asian river flowing from the Tibetan Plateau through China and Myanmar into the Andaman Sea.
Part of the Three Parallel Rivers World Heritage Site, believed to support over a quarter of the world's animal species.
One of Asia's least dammed major rivers, despite having extremely high hydropower potential.
r1159102717: An Arctic island of Russia's Chukotka region, lying astride the 180th meridian between the Chukchi and East Siberian Seas.
Home to the last known surviving population of woolly mammoths, which persisted there until about 4,000 years ago.
A strictly protected nature reserve since 1976 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2004.
p1159105103: A crescent-shaped volcanic remnant in the Tasman Sea between Australia and New Zealand, part of New South Wales.
Settled permanently in 1834 as a whaling provisioning port, later built an economy on exporting endemic kentia palms.
A UNESCO World Heritage Site, with the uninhabited volcanic spire Ball's Pyramid nearby.
m1159115811: A sea at the northern edge of the Southern Ocean, bounded by the Drake Passage and the Scotia Arc island system.
Named after the expedition ship Scotia; many icebergs melt in its waters.
r1159104079: A desert in Central Asia between the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers, split among Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.
Its name means "Red Sand" in Turkic languages.
m1159116767: A sea within the Pacific Ocean between Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands.
The site of major naval battles during World War II.
r1159104199: A mountain range running from southern British Columbia through Washington and Oregon to Northern California.
Part of the Pacific Ring of Fire; its volcanoes are responsible for every US eruption in the contiguous states in 200 years.
Mount St. Helens, part of this range, erupted dramatically in 1980.
e1159106545: The highest volcano on Earth, a dormant complex volcano on the Argentina-Chile border and the highest peak in Chile.
Hosts the highest lake of any kind in the world, a crater lake near its summit despite the mountain's extreme aridity.
Was debated for decades as a rival to Aconcagua for South America's highest peak, a question settled in Aconcagua's favor.
vQ82207: A river in Russia's Sakha Republic flowing between the Yana and Kolyma rivers.
r1159103505: The delta where the Nile spreads out and empties into the Mediterranean Sea in Lower Egypt.
One of the world's largest river deltas, stretching 240 km along the coast from Alexandria to Port Said.
r1159103473: One of the main Hawaiian Islands, nicknamed the "Garden Isle" for its lush landscape.
Home to Waimea Canyon and the dramatic Nā Pali Coast.
m1159116315: A large open gulf off the southern coast of mainland Australia, generally considered part of the Indian Ocean.
Formed about 50 million years ago when Gondwana broke apart, separating Australia from Antarctica.
Known for whale-watching along its cliff-lined coastline.
m1159117171: A gulf on China's east coast, the innermost extension of the Yellow Sea, enclosed by four Chinese provinces/municipalities.
Declared part of China's inland waters in 1958, it lies close to Beijing and Tianjin and is heavily trafficked by shipping.
r1159103413: One of the larger islands in Canada's Arctic Archipelago, separated from Victoria Island by Prince of Wales Strait.
Once home to the majority of the world's muskoxen, though disease has sharply reduced their numbers.
Had a population of just 104 people as of the 2021 census, all in the settlement of Sachs Harbour.
r1159102957: An island chain off western Scotland, the longest archipelago in the British Isles and a Gaelic-language heartland.
Was part of the Norse kingdom of the Suðreyjar for over 400 years before passing to Scotland in 1266.
The 19th-century Highland Clearances devastated many of its communities.
m1159117845: A strait between Tamil Nadu, India and Mannar Island, Sri Lanka, linking the Bay of Bengal to the Laccadive Sea.
Bordered by the chain of islets and shoals known as Ram Setu, or Adam's Bridge.
r1159103469: A Pacific atoll of Kiribati, also called Christmas Island, and one of the world's largest atolls by land area.
Lies in the world's furthest-forward time zone, UTC+14, making it among the first places to see the New Year.
Was the site of British and American nuclear weapons tests in the late 1950s and 1962.
p1159104865: An island of Trinidad and Tobago lying northeast of the larger island of Trinidad.
e1159106339: An active stratovolcano in Washington's Cascade Range, the highest mountain in that state.
Considered one of the world's most dangerous volcanoes due to its eruption potential and proximity to Seattle.
Its glacial ice could trigger massive lahars threatening river valleys home to about 80,000 people.
r1159102383: The southernmost and westernmost of Spain's Canary Islands, nicknamed "Meridian Island".
The second-smallest of the eight inhabited Canary Islands, with its capital at Valverde.
l1159113405: A freshwater lake on the Congo River's longest arm, on the border between Zambia and the DRC.
Lies between the river's Luapula and Luvua segments; its name simply means "lake" in several Bantu languages.
r1159103643: A hot desert spanning parts of Arizona, California and northwestern Mexico, home to the iconic saguaro cactus.
Distinct from nearby deserts for its subtropical winter warmth and two annual rainy seasons.
Considered a contender for the hottest desert on Earth.
p1159105087: A subantarctic island roughly halfway between Tasmania and Antarctica, governed as part of Tasmania since 1880.
Home to the entire royal penguin population during its nesting season, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
m1159116625: A strait between the Florida Keys and Cuba, connecting the Gulf of Mexico to the Atlantic Ocean.
Carries the Florida Current, the beginning of the Gulf Stream.
l1159114015: The largest freshwater lake in China, in Jiangxi Province, draining into the Yangtze River.
Its area fluctuates dramatically by season and has shrunk overall in recent years due to drought and dam operations.
Winters host up to 90% of the world's critically endangered Siberian cranes.
r1159103093: A range of medium mountains in eastern France near the German border, forming the western edge of the Upper Rhine Plain.
Its highest peak, the Grand Ballon, reaches 1,424 m.
r1159103409: The seventh-largest island in the Philippines, located off southwestern Luzon.
Divided into Occidental and Oriental Mindoro provinces, with Mount Halcon as its highest point.
r1159103825: The main island of the Autonomous Region of Bougainville in Papua New Guinea, and the largest in the Solomon Islands archipelago.
Was formerly linked to the German Empire as part of the North Solomons.
Voted for independence from Papua New Guinea in a 2019 referendum, with full independence planned for 2030.
l1159114173: Sweden's second-largest lake after Vänern, and the sixth-largest in Europe.
Relatively deep for its size, connected since 1832 via the Göta Canal to Vänern and onward to the Atlantic.
r1159103091: A highland area in northern Germany spanning Lower Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia.
Its highest peak, the Brocken, reaches 1,141 m above sea level.
r1159103993: A peninsula in Far North Queensland, Australia, the largest wilderness area in northern Australia.
In 1606, Dutch sailor Willem Janszoon became the first European to land in Australia here.
Home to eucalyptus savannahs and tropical rainforest preserved for their global ecological significance.
r1159102759: An Indonesian island in the Lesser Sunda Archipelago, roughly the size of Jamaica or Hawaii island.
Separated from Flores by the Sumba Strait and from Timor by the Savu Sea.
r1730072751: A mountain range separating the Balkan Peninsula from the Adriatic Sea, stretching from Italy to Albania.
Its highest section, the Accursed Mountains, holds the range's tallest peak, Maja Jezercë, at 2,694 m.
Formed largely of limestone and dolomite folded by the Adriatic microplate's collision with Europe.
p1159105057: A remote volcanic island of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands in the southern Indian Ocean.
The northernmost volcanic island on the Antarctic Plate, home only to a small seasonal research station.
m1159116735: A sea in the southwestern Pacific northeast of New Guinea and south of the Bismarck Archipelago, within Papua New Guinea's waters.
r1159102735: A World Heritage-listed sand island off Queensland, Australia, formerly known as Fraser Island.
Traditional land of the Butchulla people, officially renamed K'gari (meaning "Paradise") in 2023.
Visited by up to 500,000 people a year despite a tiny permanent population.
r1159104107: A vast, poorly drained plain in western Siberia between the Ural Mountains and the Yenisei River.
Home to some of the world's largest swamps and was the source of most Soviet oil and gas production in the 1970s-80s.
e1159105637: An active stratovolcano near Russia's Bering Sea coast, the highest mountain in Siberia and the highest active volcano in Eurasia.
Part of the Volcanoes of Kamchatka UNESCO World Heritage Site, almost continuously active since its first recorded eruption in 1697.
m1159120417: A small sea within Indonesia, named for Savu Island, bounded by Timor, Flores, Sumba and Rote.
Reaches depths of about 3,500 m despite its modest size.
e1159106313: The highest point in the contiguous United States, in California's Sierra Nevada range.
Its summit is the southern terminus of the 211-mile John Muir Trail from Yosemite Valley.
m1159116897: A small sea between the Indonesian islands of Buru and Seram, once known as the spice-rich South Moluccas.
A historically busy shipping route for nutmeg, cloves and peppercorns, and a tectonically active area.
r1159102733: Australia's third-largest island, in South Australia southwest of Adelaide.
Known for sea lion colonies at Seal Bay and little penguin populations.
Settled permanently from 1836 during British colonization of South Australia, with agriculture and tourism as key industries.
r1159104227: A vast mountainous plateau region of Siberia, one of Russia's major geographic regions.
r1159104535: A sub-Antarctic archipelago of small islands in the southern Indian Ocean, part of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands.
vQ124653: A river in western Siberia flowing through Kazakhstan and Russia, the main left tributary of the Irtysh.
r1159102353: An autonomous volcanic island in the Comoros archipelago in the southwestern Indian Ocean.
Historically also known in English as Johanna; its chief town is Mutsamudu.
r1730071761: A circular dome of mountains in northeastern New York State, home to Mount Marcy, the state's highest point.
Contains over 200 named lakes, including Lake Placid, amid thousands of square miles of boreal forest.
Though built from rock over a billion years old, the mountains themselves are geologically young, uplifted during recent glaciation.
e1159106019: The highest mountain in Ukraine, part of the Ukrainian Carpathians in the Chornohora region.
Its slopes hold beech and spruce forest below alpine meadows, and it is the source of the Prut River.
Became a popular tourist and extreme-sports destination from the late 19th century onward.
r1159102547: The largest island of Comoros, made up of two shield volcanoes including Mount Karthala, the country's highest point.
Home to the national capital, Moroni, and most of its population is of the Comorian ethnic group.
r1159102483: A small volcanic island south of Tokyo, part of Japan's Ogasawara Archipelago, formerly known as Sulfur Island.
Site of the fierce 1945 Battle of Iwo Jima, where both the US and Japan suffered over 20,000 casualties each.
Joe Rosenthal's photograph of the flag-raising on Mount Suribachi became an iconic image of World War II.
Returned to Japan in 1968 after US occupation; it has no permanent civilian residents today.
l1159113423: A freshwater lake on the border between Russia's Primorsky Krai and China's Heilongjiang province.
r1159102671: One of the main Hawaiian Islands, long shaped by cattle ranching, pineapple and sugarcane farming.
Home to the Kalaupapa Peninsula, where a leprosy quarantine settlement operated from 1866 to 1969, now a national historical park.
r1159104313: China's largest alluvial plain, formed by Yellow River sediment and bordered by the Yanshan and Taihang mountains.
The cradle of Chinese civilization, home to Beijing, Tianjin, and the capitals of several imperial dynasties.
One of the most densely populated and agriculturally important regions in the world.
e1159105789: The highest mountain in Afghanistan, on the border with Pakistan in the Hindu Kush range.
The westernmost 7,000 m peak in the world, accessible mainly from the Wakhan District of Afghanistan.
vQ204040: A Central European river rising in Austria's Hohe Tauern and flowing as a tributary of the Drava and Danube.
Forms part of the border between Croatia and Hungary; Graz is the largest city along its course.
r1159102543: The largest island of Cape Verde, home to half the nation's population and its capital, Praia.
Its town of Ribeira Grande, founded in 1462, was the first European settlement in the islands and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
r1159104153: A peninsula in northwest Siberia, Russia, bordered by the Kara Sea and the Gulf of Ob.
Its name means "End of the Land" in Nenets, the language of its indigenous inhabitants.
p1159104867: The largest island in Venezuela's Nueva Esparta state, off the country's northwest coast in the Caribbean Sea.
r1159102529: The southernmost island of the Kuril Islands, under Russian administration since the end of World War II.
Claimed by Japan as part of its "Northern Territories".
r1159102843: The smaller, northern major island of São Tomé and Príncipe, off the west coast of Africa in the Gulf of Guinea.
A heavily eroded volcano speculated to be over three million years old.
r1159104065: Australia's second-largest desert, straddling Western Australia's Pilbara and Kimberley regions and the Northern Territory.
e1159105775: The highest mountain in the Tian Shan range, on the border of Kyrgyzstan and China.
Part of the Kakshaal Too, the highest section of the Tian Shan, southeast of Lake Issyk-Kul.
l1159126709: Mongolia's largest lake by surface area, a highly saline body of water within its own closed basin.
A remnant of a much larger saline sea that covered the region thousands of years ago.
r1159102533: An island off the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Bering Sea.
r1159103677: A peninsula in Liaoning province, Northeast China, between the Daliao and Yalu rivers.
Encompasses the city of Dalian; its name means "Liao region's east".
e1159106509: A stratovolcano in Colombia, the highest point in both the Caldas and Tolima departments.
Its 1985 eruption triggered a lahar that destroyed the town of Armero, killing an estimated 25,000 people, the deadliest lahar on record.
Melting of its summit glaciers during eruptions continues to pose a lahar risk to nearby towns.
r1159102367: An island in Cape Verde's Sotavento group, reaching the archipelago's highest point at its active volcano, Pico do Fogo.
r1159102889: A group of eight atolls in Kiribati, between the Gilbert Islands and the Line Islands in the central Pacific.
The Phoenix Islands Protected Area, established in 2008, is one of the world's largest marine protected areas.
Essentially uninhabited except for a few families on Canton Island.
p1159105015: A peninsula extending into the Atlantic from southeastern Massachusetts, named in 1602 by Bartholomew Gosnold.
Separated from the mainland since 1914 by the Cape Cod Canal, crossed by the Sagamore and Bourne bridges.
xQ204658: The largest glacier in the Alps, in Switzerland's Bernese Alps, formed by four smaller glaciers converging at Konkordiaplatz.
Part of the Jungfrau-Aletsch UNESCO World Heritage Site, it has been rapidly retreating, losing 3.2 km of length since 1870.
m1159116861: A strait between the Strait of Malacca and the South China Sea, bordered by Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia.
One of the busiest waterways in the world, with about 2,000 merchant ships passing through daily.
r1159103775: The mainland region of Newfoundland and Labrador province, separated from the island of Newfoundland by the Strait of Belle Isle.
Makes up 71% of the province's area but only 6% of its population, home to Inuit and Innu indigenous peoples.
r1159103477: The second-largest island of Fiji, lying north of the larger Viti Levu, formerly known as Sandalwood Island.
p1159104859: The largest island of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, a volcanic island in the southern Caribbean.
Home to La Soufrière, the country's highest peak and an active volcano that erupted as recently as 2021.
Was the site of 18th-century wars between the Garifuna people and Britain before being ceded to the British.
e1159105709: The highest peak of the Altai Mountains, on the border of Russia and Kazakhstan.
Part of the Golden Mountains of Altai UNESCO World Heritage Site.
e1159107739: An active stratovolcano and the largest active volcano in New Zealand, within Tongariro National Park.
Home to the North Island's major ski resorts and only glaciers, with a crater lake between its three peaks.
r1159102363: A volcanic island in Portugal's Azores archipelago, home to Angra do Heroísmo, the archipelago's oldest city and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Hosts a major Portuguese Air Force base with a US Air Force detachment.
r1159103919: A discontinuous chain of hill ranges and plateau escarpments in west-central India, running roughly parallel to the Narmada River.
Mentioned in ancient texts as the traditional southern boundary of Āryāvarta, the Vedic cultural region.
p1159105171: A peninsula in Senegal and the westernmost point of the African mainland.
Home to Dakar, Senegal's capital, which occupies its southern tip.
r1159102375: The third largest island of Cape Verde, a desert-like island known for its beaches and sea turtles.
The easternmost Cape Verde island, closest to the African mainland.
r1730072563: The southwestern coastal region of India, covering Kerala and parts of Karnataka.
Home to Kuttanad, India's lowest-elevation point, where farming takes place below sea level.
The first part of India to receive rain from the Southwest monsoon's Arabian Sea branch.
e1159105965: The highest peak in Estonia and the Baltic states, located in the gently hilly Haanja Upland near the Latvian and Russian borders.
l1159115043: The largest lake located entirely within Estonia, and the country's second-largest overall after Lake Peipus.
Drains via the Emajõgi River into Lake Peipus.
r1159102435: A solitary raised coral island of Kiribati, formerly known as Ocean Island, the westernmost point of the country.
One of the Pacific's important phosphate-rich elevated islands, along with Nauru and Makatea.
r1159103017: A mountainous region on Sydney's western outskirts in New South Wales, Australia, part of the Great Dividing Range.
Opened to British settlement by the 1813 Blaxland, Wentworth and Lawson expedition.
Severely affected by major bushfires since the early 2010s, yet still drew 8.4 million visitors in 2018.
r1159104371: One of Antarctica's two major regions, including the Antarctic Peninsula and separated from East Antarctica by the Transantarctic Mountains.
Covered by the West Antarctic Ice Sheet, with the Antarctic Peninsula's west coast among the fastest-warming places on Earth.
p1159105101: An uninhabited rocky islet near Lord Howe Island, the eroded plug of a shield volcano formed 6.4 million years ago.
The tallest volcanic sea stack in the world, and home to the Lord Howe Island stick insect, rediscovered in 2001 after being presumed extinct.
l1159126815: The second-largest lake in Turkey and one of the largest hypersaline lakes in the world, in the Central Anatolia Region.
Dried up completely in October 2021 due to climate change and unsustainable irrigation.
vQ2216: A river in Alberta, Canada, rising at the Columbia Icefield and flowing into Lake Athabasca.
Designated a Canadian Heritage River, with scenic Athabasca Falls located along its course.
m1159118493: A bight on the west-central African coast, at the easternmost part of the Gulf of Guinea.
Marks the point where Africa's coastline turns from a north-south to an east-west orientation.
r1159103395: The largest island of Palawan province in the Philippines, bordered by the South China Sea and the Sulu Sea.
Known for abundant wildlife, jungle mountains and white sandy beaches that draw tourists and developers.
r1159104229: An inland plateau in East Asia spanning Mongolia and parts of China and Russia, including the Gobi Desert.
Bounded by the Greater Hinggan, Yin, Altai, Sayan and Khentii mountains, forming the heart of the Mongol homeland.
e1159106835: The highest mountain in Ireland, on the Iveragh Peninsula at the center of the MacGillycuddy's Reeks range.
Composed mainly of sandstone, with glacially carved features like the Eagle's Nest corrie popular with climbers.
Most commonly climbed via the Devil's Ladder route; access is by landowner permission, as it lies outside any national park.
vQ2220: Rises in the Rocky Mountains of British Columbia and flows northeast through Alberta to join the Athabasca River.
Together with the Finlay and Slave rivers, forms part of the 13th-longest river system in the world, feeding the Mackenzie River.
m1159119095: A shallow, highly saline lagoon off the Caspian Sea in northwestern Turkmenistan.
Separated from the Caspian by a narrow rocky ridge through which seawater flows in, evaporating in its salt pans.
r1159102857: The largest island of Portugal's Madeira Archipelago, the summit of a massive submerged shield volcano in the Atlantic.
Formed by volcanic activity beginning over five million years ago, with its most recent eruptions just 6,500 years ago.
Its central mountain ridge peaks at Pico Ruivo, 1,862 m, with steep ravines shaping where its villages sit.
r1159103987: The region of southwestern Vietnam where the Mekong River empties into the sea through a network of distributaries.
Settled as early as the 4th century BC and shaped by Khmer, Vietnamese, Chinese and French influence.
A biologically rich region where over 1,000 animal species were recorded between 1997 and 2007, but vulnerable to sea level rise.
r1159103487: A chain of islands in the southwestern Philippines, forming the border between the Sulu and Celebes seas.
Home to the indigenous Tausug and Sama peoples, including the seafaring Bajau, and formerly the seat of the Sultanate of Sulu.
e1159105283: The highest mountain in Ethiopia, located within Simien Mountains National Park.
e1159108707: The highest mountain in Venezuela, named after independence hero Simón Bolívar, reachable only on foot.
The Mérida cable car, once the world's highest and longest, reaches a neighboring peak from which climbers continue to the summit.
l1159123091: A freshwater lake in East Kazakhstan, the largest in its region, frozen from November to April.
Its shrinkage has been stabilized since it became part of the Bukhtarma Hydroelectric Power Plant's reservoir.
r1159102355: An island off the coast of Tanzania, the main island of the Mafia Archipelago, administratively separate from Zanzibar.
Its economy relies on fishing and subsistence farming, with growing tourism from scuba divers and birdwatchers.
r1159103379: The largest island of Russia's Severnaya Zemlya group in the Arctic, named after the Russian Revolution.
Half covered by glaciers reaching into the sea, rising to 965 m at Mount Karpinsky.
r1159103495: An archipelago off British Columbia, Canada, formerly called the Queen Charlotte Islands, renamed in 2010 to honor the Haida people.
Home to the Haida Nation for 13,000 years; in 2024 British Columbia transferred title of over 200 islands back to the Haida.
Separated from the mainland by the Hecate Strait, with Graham and Moresby as its two main islands.
e1159108681: An active stratovolcano in Colombia near the city of Pasto, currently the country's most active volcano.
A 1993 eruption killed nine people, including six scientists studying the crater to help predict future eruptions.
r1730070385: A group of 52 coral islets forming the smallest of Tokelau's three atolls, in the south Pacific.
The northernmost territory under New Zealand sovereignty.
r1159103519: A coastal region on the southeastern Indian peninsula, bounded by the Bay of Bengal and backed by the Eastern Ghats.
Named after the Chola dynasty's realm, Cholamandalam; known in medieval Muslim sources as the Ma'bar Coast.
e1159105501: The highest mountain on the Indochinese peninsula, nicknamed "the Roof of Indochina", in Vietnam's Hoang Lien Son range.
e1159106029: A 100-km mountain range in the Dinaric Alps on the Bosnia-Croatia border, composed of limestone and dolomite.
Its peak Sinjal/Dinara gives the whole Dinaric Alps their name; Troglav is the range's actual highest point.
l1159113531: A freshwater lake in northern Zambia whose name means "where the water meets the sky", surrounded by vast wetlands.
Sits in the upper Congo River basin; its largest tributary, the Chambeshi, is the ultimate source of the Congo River.
m1159117973: A gulf on Tunisia's east coast in the Mediterranean, also known as the Lesser Syrtis, spanning from Sfax to Djerba.
Known for unusually large tides for the Mediterranean and for sponge and tuna fisheries at its ports.
r1159103573: A major east-west mountain range in southern Shaanxi, China, dividing the Yangtze and Yellow River drainage basins.
Forms the natural boundary between North and South China and has historically blocked nomadic invasions from the north.
Its highest peak, Mount Taibai, reaches 3,767 m near the ancient capital Xi'an.
r1159103947: A series of mountain ranges stretching along North America's West Coast from Alaska to central Mexico.
Part of the North American Cordillera, including the Coast Mountains, Cascade Range and California Coast Ranges.
vQ686021: A river in western Pennsylvania and New York, the chief tributary of the Ohio River, joining it at Pittsburgh.
Historically considered by Native Americans and settlers to be the upper Ohio River itself.
m1159116553: A large inlet of the Caribbean Sea along Mexico, Belize, Guatemala and Honduras.
Lined by the Belize Barrier Reef, part of the second-largest coral reef system in the world.
Was a haunt of the pirate Blackbeard during the winter of 1717-18.
r1159103751: A broad, flat valley running through the interior of California, bounded by the Coast Ranges and Sierra Nevada.
One of the most agriculturally productive regions in the US, supplying much of the country's fruits, vegetables and nuts.
Its Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys meet at a delta that empties into San Francisco Bay.
l1159114391: Sweden's fourth-largest lake, draining through Lake Mälaren to the Baltic Sea near Stockholm.
Rebel leader Engelbrekt Engelbrektsson was assassinated on an islet in the lake in 1436.
m1159115921: A sheltered part of the North Atlantic off northwest Scotland, between the mainland/Inner Hebrides and the Outer Hebrides.
Designated a Marine Protected Area in 2020 to protect basking sharks and minke whales.
r1159103555: A mountain chain in northeastern Siberia between the Yana and Indigirka rivers, home to traditional Yakut cultural sites.
Its highest peak, Peak Pobeda, reaches 3,003 m.
l1159106843: A lake in the Canadian province of Manitoba, northwest of the capital Winnipeg, among the world's 35 largest lakes.
r1159103515: The world's largest river delta, covering the Bengal region of Bangladesh and India's West Bengal.
Formed by the combined waters of the Ganges and Brahmaputra rivers emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
Among the most fertile regions on Earth, earning the nickname the "Green Delta".
r1159104035: A desert plateau region centered on the Four Corners area of the southwestern United States.
Drained mostly by the Colorado River, it contains the Grand Canyon and nine US national parks including Zion and Arches.
Known as "Red Rock Country" for its colorful, eroded sandstone formations.
xQ672241: A segmented waterfall on the Sharavati River in Karnataka, India, plunging about 253 m into four distinct cascades.
The third-highest waterfall in India by total height, a major tourist attraction with two viewpoints.
r1159103721: A hyperarid basin in Qinghai Province, China, about a quarter of which is covered by saline lakes and playas.
l1159106781: The largest freshwater lake entirely within the contiguous United States (excluding the connected Great Lakes), in Florida.
Exceptionally shallow for its size, averaging just 9 feet deep, fed primarily by the Kissimmee River.
Its center is the only point in the US where more than four counties meet.
xQ654352: The largest glacier in continental Europe, in Vestland county, Western Norway.
Its highest peak, Lodalskåpa, reaches 2,083 m.
r1730073011: An administrative region in southeastern Somalia covering the city of Mogadishu, the country's capital.
The only Somali region that does not belong to any of the country's seven federal states.
r1159104027: A highland region in southwest China spanning Yunnan and Guizhou provinces.
Flatter plateau terrain in the southwest gives way to mountainous karst topography in the northeast.
l1159106825: A lake spanning Ontario and Manitoba, Canada, and Minnesota, USA, containing over 14,552 islands.
The sixth-largest freshwater lake partly within the United States, separating Minnesota's Northwest Angle from the rest of the country.
Provides nesting habitat for piping plovers and American white pelicans.
l1159114573: A lake in northwestern Vologda Oblast, Russia, the second-largest natural lake in the region and among Europe's ten biggest.
The town of Belozersk sits on its shore.
xQ1542432: The second-largest body of ice in the world, covering about 80% of Greenland's surface.
Averages 1,673 m thick and reaches over 3,488 m at its deepest point.
Now losing ice at the fastest rate in at least 12,000 years due to greenhouse gas emissions.
r1159104055: A flat, arid plain on Australia's Great Australian Bight coast, the world's largest single exposure of limestone bedrock.
Stretches about 1,100 km across the border between South Australia and Western Australia.
l1159123217: A lake on Russia's Kola Peninsula just beyond the Arctic Circle, with three interconnected basins.
Known for its clear water and abundant fish; drains via the Niva River into the White Sea.
m1159120759: A marginal sea of the Pacific between British Columbia and Washington state, including the Strait of Georgia and Puget Sound.
Partially sheltered from the open Pacific by Vancouver Island and the Olympic Peninsula.
Anchored by Vancouver to the north and Seattle to the south, home to 8.76 million people.
p1159105173: A peninsula in far northeastern Tunisia, known in antiquity as the Cape of Mercury.
l1159126845: A lake in the Main Ethiopian Rift, reddish-brown from suspended sediment, with the town of Arba Minch on its shore.
Briefly renamed Lake Margherita in 1896 after the Italian queen by explorer Vittorio Bottego.
r1159102603: A 56-km quartzite scarp in South Africa running through Johannesburg, named "white water ridge" in Afrikaans for its waterfalls.
Its gold deposits gave the South African currency, the rand, its name in 1961.
Forms a continental divide, with runoff draining to both the Indian and Atlantic Oceans.
r1159103949: A mountain range in northeastern Mexico, part of the American Cordillera backbone running through the Americas.
l1159107251: Mexico's largest freshwater lake since Lake Texcoco dried up in the early 17th century.
Straddles the states of Jalisco and Michoacán.
xQ495475: A waterfall on the White Nile in Uganda, where the river squeezes through a 7 m gap before tumbling 43 m into Lake Albert.
Named by explorer Samuel Baker after Roderick Murchison of the Royal Geographical Society.
Briefly renamed Kabalega Falls under Idi Amin's regime; Ernest Hemingway crashed a plane nearby in 1954.
m1159118151: A large Pacific Ocean inlet between Ecuador and Peru, named after the city of Guayaquil.
Underlain by active geological faults capable of generating dangerous earthquakes.
r1159104251: A semi-arid shrubland and thorn-forest ecoregion in interior northeastern Brazil, named "white forest" in Old Tupi.
The only biome found exclusively in Brazil, home to 26 million people and over 2,000 species found nowhere else.
r1159103177: A peninsula projecting into the Sea of Japan from Ishikawa Prefecture on Japan's main island of Honshu.
Its main industries are agriculture, fisheries and tourism.
r1159104193: A mountain range stretching across northern Alaska into Canada's Yukon, about 126 million years old.
Crossed by the Dalton Highway and Trans-Alaska Pipeline en route to the Prudhoe Bay oil fields.
Home to the Red Dog mine, the largest zinc mine in the world.
m1159116967: A 180-mile inlet stretching from the Gulf of Alaska to Anchorage, branching into the Knik and Turnagain arms.
Alaska's most populated watershed, fed by glacial rivers and home to the active volcano Mount Redoubt.
r1159103549: A mountain range of volcanoes running along the center of Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula.
Its highest peak, Ichinsky, a stratovolcano, reaches 3,607 m; small glaciers still cling to the range.
r1159103903: A mountain range forming the border between Qinghai and Gansu provinces in China, an outlier of the Kunlun Mountains.
m1159117797: Norway's third-longest fjord, stretching 130 km through Trøndelag county past the city of Trondheim.
Has the largest biological production of any Norwegian fjord, with deep-water corals discovered near Trondheim.
Was an important waterway during the Viking Age and remains so today.
r1159103173: A mountainous peninsula extending from the Arabian Peninsula between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.
Divided between the United Arab Emirates and Oman, overlooking the Strait of Hormuz.
r1159104029: A plateau in northeastern Thailand's Isan region, named after the city of Nakhon Ratchasima.
p1159104881: A headland on the coast of Moroccan-occupied Western Sahara, whose original Arabic name means "father of danger".
Marked a historic barrier that European sailors feared rounding for centuries.
r1159103121: A high, almost entirely volcanic mountain range in eastern Alaska, within Wrangell-St. Elias National Park.
Includes Mount Blackburn and Mount Sanford, the second- and third-highest volcanoes in the US.
Named for Mount Wrangell, one of the largest andesite shield volcanoes in the world and the range's only active volcano.
r1159104091: A fertile lowland basin in southwestern China, anchored by Chengdu and Chongqing and drained by the upper Yangtze.
Supports over 100 million people and is considered the breadbasket of China for its rice cultivation.
xQ278245: The world's largest glacier, in East Antarctica, draining 8% of the Antarctic ice sheet northward to the Amery Ice Shelf.
About 96 km wide and over 435 km long, named in 1957 after Australian mapping director Bruce Lambert.
xQ983252: A pair of waterfalls on the Quây Sơn River straddling the China-Vietnam border.
Located north of Hanoi between the karst hills of Guangxi and Cao Bằng Province.
r1159103311: A large mesa, known as the Staked Plains, spanning eastern New Mexico and northwestern Texas.
One of the largest tablelands in North America, rising steadily from 3,000 to over 5,000 feet in elevation.
xQ1101379: A waterfall on the Kunene River in northern Namibia, 120 m high and up to 700 m wide in full flood.
Among the largest waterfalls in Africa by both volume and width.
r1730070763: A large endorheic salt pan in northern Namibia, the centerpiece of Etosha National Park, the country's second-largest wildlife park.
Mostly dry, but floods with a thin, heavily salted layer of water after heavy rains.
r1159103215: A remote sandstone plateau in southwest Egypt and southeast Libya, whose name means "the Great Barrier".
Known for dramatic cliff paintings and rock carvings depicting an earlier, more fertile era.
r1159103275: A desert in the Lake Eyre Basin spanning South Australia, Queensland and New South Wales.
One of three deserts, alongside the Tirari and Simpson, occupying parts of the Lake Eyre Basin.
r1730072041: A desert region in Oman named for the Bani Wahiba tribe, formerly known as Wahiba Sands.
A 1986 Royal Geographical Society expedition documented over 16,000 invertebrate species and 150 plant species there.
xQ1434582: A glacier in the Himalaya of southern Tibet, fed by Mount Everest and flowing north through the Rongbuk Valley.
Home to the Rongbuk Monastery at its northern end, the highest monastery in the world.
xQ962630: A large valley glacier on Argentina's Southern Patagonian Ice Field, within Los Glaciares National Park.
Named after Sweden's Uppsala University, which sponsored early glaciological studies in the area.
Known for its rapid, accelerating retreat since being first documented in 1810.
xQ40417: A waterfall on Stony Creek in Queensland's UNESCO-listed Wet Tropics, Australia's tallest single-drop waterfall at 268 m.
xQ1635297: A waterfall on the Snake River in Idaho, nicknamed the "Niagara of the West" for being taller than Niagara Falls.
Formed by catastrophic flooding from ancient Lake Bonneville about 14,000 years ago.
Historically marked the upper limit of salmon migration on the Snake River and was an important Native American fishing site.
